name: Morano Electric

domains.result: HTTP 200, no redirect; the real Morano Electric site (home page, service pages, four regional phone numbers, callback form). HTTPS loaded in Chrome without a certificate warning. http://moranoelectric.com/ and https://www.moranoelectric.com/ both served the same page. At 390 px the header shows only logo and hamburger; the header phone is not displayed.

domains.role: site file — injected spam sitemap entries
domains.result: File allows all crawlers but contains 192 sitemap lines, 128 of them pointing at .php files (groupon.php, recollection.php) that are not part of this static site. Sampled entries (groupon.php?sitemapindex.xml, recollection.php?sitemapindex.xml, sitemap832.xml) all return HTTP 404.

links_to_broken_domain.place: Google Business Profile — website field shows moranoelectric.com and the link loads the live site (not broken); profile is complete with Electrician category, 23 Serviss Ave, 'Open 24 hours', 4.7 from 103 reviews, newest review about a month old

likely_cause.reasoning: The business's own pages are intact, but robots.txt was rewritten with 192 sitemap lines, 128 of them pointing at .php files that do not exist on this HTML site and now return 404 — the footprint of an injected spam-sitemap campaign on the hosting account. A 26 Jan 2022 Wayback capture of robots.txt was clean (four lines, 'Disallow:'); the injected version was already present in a 25 Jul 2025 capture. The domain itself is not lapsed or parked: GoDaddy registration runs to 25 Oct 2027, with client delete/renew/transfer/update prohibited. A 10 Dec 2021 capture of the domain was a GoDaddy parking lander, so the site only appears in captures from Feb 2024 onward. Nobody has said publicly who made the change or when, so cause is inference from the file contents and archive dates.

fix_steps.step: Ask the web host (nameservers are ns1/ns2.newwebdesign.com) for a malware scan and a list of files changed in the last 18 months, and remove anything the business did not add.
fix_steps.who: Web host, working with whoever maintains the site

fix_steps.step: Replace robots.txt with a short clean file and create a real sitemap.xml; the existing human sitemap is sitemap.html and the XML files the current robots.txt points to do not exist (all 404).

Change every password that can write to the site — hosting/SFTP, the PHP mail script that receives the callback form, and the mail account published on the site — add two-factor, and check the mailbox for forwarding rules or filters the owner did not set.
Keep the domain registration locked, funded and on auto-renew, and confirm the registrant email address still reaches the owner; the domain is already client-locked and paid to 2027-10-25.

Check Google Search Console for security issues and for the injected URLs, submit the new sitemap, and tidy the customer-facing details found in the same pass: the contact page spells the street 'service ave' instead of Serviss Ave, the title tag is only 'MORANO Electric' with no meta description, and 'EMMERGENCY' is misspelled.

after_fix.opportunity: Add an estimate-request form (service, town, preferred time, optional photo) to the contact page, and keep a tap-to-call button visible in the mobile header.
after_fix.evidence: The hero 'LEARN MORE' button on the home page points at contact.html, and that page has no form at all — only the phone number and the address. At 390 px the header phone is hidden, so a mobile visitor's first call button sits far down the home page.

severity_reason: Customers who visit today see the real, working site, so there is no visible breakage, and the domain is paid up and locked. But files on the site's server were edited without the owner's intent and the leftover sitemap spam still points 192 URLs at the domain; the same server receives the only web lead form, and the published business mailbox is a free Gmail address, so an unresolved compromise is worth closing out.
audit_md:
# Website Health Check: Morano Electric

## What we saw on 13 November 2026

- moranoelectric.com loads normally (HTTP 200, valid certificate): the full business site with services, four regional phone numbers and a callback form.
- Its robots.txt has been overwritten with 192 sitemap lines; 128 point at .php files (groupon.php, recollection.php) that do not exist on this HTML site. Each one we tested returns 404.
- That robots.txt was clean in a 26 January 2022 archive capture and already injected by 25 July 2025.
- The domain is still registered through GoDaddy, paid to 25 October 2027 and transfer-locked. The Google listing (23 Serviss Ave, Electrician, 4.7 from 103 reviews) links to it and shows reviews from the past month.

## What it means for customers

A customer who taps the site today gets the real Morano Electric pages, so nothing looks wrong from outside. The change was made on the server that also receives the callback form, so it is worth closing out rather than leaving.

## How to fix it

1. Have the host scan the account and list recently changed files (2-4 hours).
2. Replace robots.txt and publish a real sitemap.xml (1-2 hours).
3. Change hosting, mail and form-script passwords, add two-factor, check mailbox forwarding (1-2 hours).
4. Keep the domain locked, funded and auto-renewing at the registrar (0.5-1 hour).
5. Clear the injected URLs in Search Console, submit the new sitemap, fix the contact-page street name and page titles (1-3 hours).

## After the fix

Put an estimate-request form on the contact page. The home page's main "LEARN MORE" button points there and the page has no form at all, while at phone width the header phone is hidden.

---

Prepared from publicly available information on 13 November 2026. We did not log in to or change anything.

## Outreach email draft

Subject: Your site loads fine — but its robots.txt has been rewritten

Hello — I looked at moranoelectric.com the way a customer would this week: it loads fine, but its robots.txt has been overwritten with roughly 190 sitemap links to files that do not exist on your site, which usually means someone edited files on your hosting account. I have desktop and phone screenshots of what a visitor sees today, plus a short list of the handful of things worth checking, starting with your host's recently changed files and that robots.txt. If it is useful I can show you the screenshots and walk through the list — no obligation either way.

## Walk-in / phone opener

I work with local businesses on their websites — did you know your site's robots.txt has been filled with injected sitemap links to files that aren't there, which usually means your hosting account was touched?

## Sources

- https://moranoelectric.com/ (home page, live check, screenshots site-desktop-2026-11-13.png and site-mobile-390-2026-11-13.png)
- https://moranoelectric.com/robots.txt (192 sitemap lines, 128 to .php files; screenshot robots-txt-spam-2026-11-13.png)
- https://moranoelectric.com/contact.html (no form; address written as '23 service ave')
- https://moranoelectric.com/sitemap.html (the real page list)
- https://rdap.org/domain/moranoelectric.com (registered 2021-10-25, expires 2027-10-25, last changed 2025-10-26, GoDaddy, client-lock statuses, NS newwebdesign.com)
- https://www.google.com/maps/place/Morano+Electric/@40.4656933,-74.4047997,17z (website field, address, phone, 4.7/103, newest review about a month old)
- https://web.archive.org/web/20211210101943id_/http://moranoelectric.com/ (Dec 2021 capture was a GoDaddy parking lander)
- https://web.archive.org/web/20220126162056id_/http://moranoelectric.com/robots.txt (clean robots.txt, Jan 2022)
- https://web.archive.org/web/20250725015011id_/https://www.moranoelectric.com/robots.txt (already injected, Jul 2025)
- http://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=moranoelectric.com&output=json&from=2019&to=2026 (capture list, 2021-2025)
- https://reviews.birdeye.com/electric-morano-inc-167002699129521 (listing as 'Electric Morano Inc', same address, unclaimed, 4.5/119)

## Open questions

- Who holds the GoDaddy account, and is the registrant email address one the owner still reads?
- Who built and who now maintains the site (the nameservers belong to newwebdesign.com)?
- Has the host seen other changes on the account, and does the callback form's mail script still send where the owner expects?
- Did the business use a different domain before 2021, and does it own any other domains still printed on old cards or ads?
- Is the Google listing claimed by the business, and does the owner control the Gmail address published on the site?
caveats: No hijacked, parked or for-sale domain was found in this case: moranoelectric.com resolves, serves the business's own site, and the Google profile links to it.

In the test browser, the page title of both the site and Google Maps showed a leading horse emoji; the raw HTML and every script file on the site contain no such character, so this is an artifact of the test browser, not the site. The earlier triage note about an emoji-only page title could not be confirmed; the HTML title is plain 'MORANO Electric'.
Cause is inferred from the robots.txt contents and archive dates; no source states who edited the file or when exactly.
The December 2021 archive capture of the domain was a GoDaddy parking lander, so the domain was parked then; public records do not show who registered it on 2021-10-25.
The callback form was not submitted, so it is unknown whether it still delivers mail.
data_gaps: BBB, Angi and HomeAdvisor returned HTTP 403 to automated requests, so those listings could not be read.
The Internet Archive CDX endpoint went offline partway through the check; only 8 home-page captures and 3 robots.txt captures were seen.
No access to the hosting account, so the extent of the change (and whether anything else was modified) is unknown.
Google Safe Browsing and Search Console status are not publicly visible and were not checked.
No Facebook or Yelp profile was found for this business in search results, so those links could not be verified.
